polished.issue: Korean sentence is grammatical and idiomatic — 쌀(uncooked rice) + 로(instrumental) + 밥을 짓다(cook rice/make a meal) is the canonical collocation. However, the English gloss 'Mother cooks rice from grains' collapses the very 쌀(uncooked)/밥(cooked) distinction the example sentence exists to teach: a learner cannot tell which Korean word is the headword 쌀, and 'grains' is an unidiomatic stand-in for 'uncooked rice'. Re-gloss to preserve the contrast.
polished.suggestion: Mother cooks rice (밥) from raw rice (쌀).

polished.issue: 이브이 is a direct transliteration of English 'Eevee' (itself read from 'Ev' of Evolution) — Korean Wikipedia and Bulbapedia confirm it is a borrowed proper noun, not a Korean root/morpheme. The shared component across the Eeveelution naming pattern (이브이 Eevee, 에브이 Espeon) is 브이 alone, not 이브이; Espeon's 에 prefix comes from 에스퍼/ESP. So both fields of the seed entry are wrong: the part of speech 'root/morpheme' overstates productivity, and treating 이브이 as a component of 에브이 is etymologically incorrect.

suggestion.gloss: Eevee (Pokémon proper noun, transliterated from English 'Eevee' < 'Ev' of Evolution); the productive shared component in the Eeveelution naming pattern is 브이, not 이브이
